reviewedBehavior.finding: First accepted PCM write remains one native buffer. Follow-up changes only the subsequent write multiplier from four to eight native buffers; frame alignment, byte-count advancement, padding and generation checks remain unchanged.

Logical paused state is set before capturing the pending write. Serialized pause waits for that write while native rendering remains running, using the existing 1000 ms bound. Generation is checked before waiting and again before native pause. Failure cleanup wakes playback only for the same generation.

Stop invalidates the generation and wakes a paused writer. Pending-write assignment precedes the observer, so replacement triggered by the observer captures that exact write. Completion callbacks remain behind the generation check; stop retains its flush, settle, flush sequence.
Short transport tails are padded with complete silent frames. File bytes remain unchanged, and offset advances by the accepted source-byte count.

Original four checks remain. Fifth check replaces once after observing a write larger than the accepted onset write, requires ordered old/new onset callbacks, one completion and no failures. Existing pause/resume completion window remains recording.durationMs + 5000 ms.

For native result objects emitted by AudioControls.ets, the exact five-check all-mode guard rejects missing, extra or duplicate check names, failed checks and a non-passed native status. The rejection branch persists status=failed and runnerValidationError before raising. The finally block reads that persisted status into the artifact; guard failures can no longer leave its status as passed. Tail mode still expects only the tail check.

primarySourceAssessment.legacyBatching: OpenHarmony 6.0 NapiAudioRenderer::Write creates one asynchronous work item per entire ArrayBuffer. WriteArrayBufferToNative loops natively rather than dispatching a separate JS promise per native buffer. Larger batches can therefore amortize bridge scheduling, allocation and completion overhead; native writable-frame waits remain.
primarySourceAssessment.pauseInference: In the inspected 6.0 implementation, WriteCacheData may copy part of a buffer before a state change causes ERR_ILLEGAL_STATE. Outer Write returns that negative result; the NAPI bridge breaks and resolves its accumulated byte count. Loss of an interrupted inner write's partial count could cause the application to retry already-queued PCM. Settling the write before native pause avoids this source-level accounting hazard.
primarySourceAssessment.zeroWriteSpinClaim: Not established. The native bridge retries a zero return, but the inspected normal paused path returns a negative state error. No claim of a confirmed paused native zero-write spin or runtime root cause is made.
primarySourceAssessment.callbackAlternative: API 20 exposes on('writeData', callback), off('writeData', callback?), and AudioRendererWriteDataCallback = (data: ArrayBuffer) => AudioDataCallbackResult | void. The native callback path uses a thread-safe JS callback, enqueues after callback return, and waits up to 1000 ms for callback completion. It avoids one NapiAsyncWork write promise per supplied chunk, but remains sensitive to JS scheduling. Callback PCM still follows ProcessWriteInner -> WriteInner -> WriteCacheData, and WaitForBufferNeedWrite also uses WRITE_CACHE_TIMEOUT_IN_MS=1500. Switching to writeData does not bypass native ring-buffer backpressure or establish a recovery from it.
primarySourceAssessment.nativeWriteTimeout: In the inspected OpenHarmony 6.0 source, WriteCacheData waits for state != RUNNING or positive writable-frame capacity, using a 1500 ms normal-stream timeout. A timeout returns a negative error and emits 'write data time out, mode is normal'. The legacy NAPI loop breaks on that error but resolves its accumulated written count, potentially zero. Repeated approximately 1500 ms zero-byte promises are consistent with this path; timing alone does not confirm that the 6.1 runtime took it.
primarySourceAssessment.runningVersusProgress: StartAudioStream waits for a server RUNNING acknowledgement, not an advancing ring read position. Ordinary pause/resume does not reset the ring; FlushBeforeStart resets frame accounting only when flushAfterStop_ is set. Server consumption advances the shared read frame, and SetCurReadFrame wakes waiting writers. Thus RUNNING is not proof of actual buffer consumption. The inspected full-write path calls UpdatePosition only after completing WriteCacheData; source review alone does not identify why any runtime consumer became slow or stalled.
primarySourceAssessment.timestampVersusPosition: Installed API 20 declares getAudioTime()/Sync() as the monotonic timestamp of the latest frame passed by the framework, with imperfect device-latency handling. It is not elapsed playback duration. API 19 getAudioTimestampInfo()/Sync() returns {framePos, timestamp}; the inspected implementation requires RUNNING, and flush or route changes reset position accounting. A stable framePos can help diagnose progress, but wall-clock or getAudioTime subtraction cannot establish an exact PCM resume offset. These API and source semantics do not certify sample-exact recovery after a runtime stall.
primarySourceAssessment.partialWriteOnNegativeReturn: WriteCacheData may copy PCM and advance the shared write position before a later timeout or state error returns a negative result without its partial byte count. The outer legacy NAPI count can therefore remain zero despite partial native copying. Retrying an entire slice can duplicate queued PCM; skipping a slice can omit PCM. A zero return is not proof that nothing was copied. Flush/recreation from a guessed offset is not certified as preserving the exact playback position.
callbackCaveats: Official documentation forbids calling AudioRenderer APIs inside the writeData callback. Fill the supplied buffer synchronously and do not mutate it after return.
Fill the last callback buffer with PCM plus silent padding; returning INVALID discards that callback buffer.

The inspected native render-mode switch requires PREPARED or NEW and cannot switch from callback mode back to normal. Existing prewarming pauses the renderer, so callback registration would need to happen earlier or on a fresh renderer.

A migration would require separate generation-aware callback cancellation, external pause/resume/drain scheduling and renewed onset measurement. A callback invocation occurs before native enqueue, unlike the existing accepted-write promise measurement.
primarySourceAssessment.practicalBoundary: The current reviewed batch is eight native buffers. Only for the observed 20 ms native buffer does this mean 160 ms of PCM; the first write remains 20 ms under that same observation. Actual duration scales with the renderer-reported buffer size and PCM byte rate. Eight buffers are not a universal 160 ms limit, and PCM duration is not a bound on asynchronous completion under CPU load. The 1000 ms settlement deadline remains unchanged; no universal guarantee that a write settles inside it is made.
primarySourceAssessment.versionBoundary: Source interpretation uses official OpenHarmony-6.0-Release and installed API 20 declarations. Project toolchain metadata identifies the tested emulator as OpenHarmony 6.1.0.31, runtime API 23. These sources do not prove that the emulator executes identical native code.

sourceResearchAddendum.method: Additional read-only inspection of official OpenHarmony-6.0-Release source and installed API 20 declarations. Only this review JSON was changed. No application changes, native tests, emulator actions or audio measurements were performed by the reviewer.
sourceResearchAddendum.scopeBoundary: This addendum extends platform-source interpretation only. It does not review or certify subsequent uncommitted diagnostic instrumentation, rebuilt HAPs, sink changes, routing restoration, or runtime outcomes. Existing source hashes and review identity remain unchanged.
sourceResearchAddendum.conclusion: Native ring-buffer timeout is a plausible explanation of the reported 1500 ms zero-byte pattern. Callback mode shares the same underlying wait, and RUNNING does not establish progress. No runtime root cause or successful repair is certified.
